content.value_statement: Interface motion often feels slow, distracting, or inaccessible when timing and tools are chosen without a clear process. This skill produces focused implementations with proven animation recipes.
actual_capabilities: Determines whether an interface action should animate based on frequency, purpose, and user context.
Selects CSS transitions, CSS animations, WAAPI, or Motion according to the interaction requirements.
Implements entrances, exits, gestures, state changes, and common component motion from documented recipes.
Applies defined easing curves, duration ranges, spring settings, and interruption behavior.
Includes reduced-motion alternatives and pointer-aware hover gating with each implementation.
limitations: It builds new animation implementations but does not audit an entire codebase.
It does not replace component libraries for accessibility, focus management, or interaction semantics.
Some visual tuning still requires playback, device testing, and human judgment.
Its recipes focus on web interface motion using CSS, JavaScript, and Motion.

use_cases.title: Add Responsive Product Motion
use_cases.description: Create subtle feedback, entrances, and state transitions that keep daily workflows responsive.

use_cases.title: Translate Motion Specs
use_cases.description: Convert interaction intent into implementation choices with explicit properties, curves, durations, and accessibility behavior.

use_cases.title: Prototype Gesture Interactions
use_cases.description: Build interruptible drag, dismissal, drawer, and spring behavior from practical recipes.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Simple State Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Add appropriate motion to this button state change. Choose the tool, properties, easing, duration, and reduced-motion behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused interface transition

prompt_templates.title: Build a Component Entrance
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the entrance and exit motion for this popover. Preserve accessibility and existing design tokens. Explain the animation gate result briefly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate component animation using an existing codebase

prompt_templates.title: Create an Interruptible Gesture
prompt_templates.prompt: Build drag-to-dismiss behavior for this panel. Include velocity handling, pointer capture, boundary damping, multi-touch protection, and reduced motion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced gesture implementation with interruption handling

prompt_templates.title: Design a Motion System Extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Add motion to this workflow without creating parallel tokens. Select the cheapest suitable tools and implement every accepted transition with accessibility variants.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced integration across several related interface states

output_examples.input: Add animation when a settings popover opens and closes.
output_examples.output: A 200 millisecond opacity and scale transition uses the existing ease-out token, trigger-based origin, symmetric exit, and reduced-motion fallback.

output_examples.input: Animate a command palette opened hundreds of times each day.
output_examples.output: No animation is added because the interaction is frequent and keyboard initiated. The palette changes state immediately.

output_examples.input: Create drag-to-dismiss motion for a mobile sheet.
output_examples.output: The sheet tracks direct transforms, uses velocity and distance thresholds, captures the pointer, resists over-drag, and settles with a spring.

best_practices: State the animation purpose before selecting tools, timing, or visual properties.
Reuse existing motion tokens and prefer transform and opacity for smooth rendering.
Test interruption, reduced motion, touch behavior, and perceived timing on real devices.
anti_patterns: Do not animate frequent keyboard actions or functional data without a clear user benefit.
Do not install a motion library when a CSS transition meets the requirements.
Do not ship broad transition declarations, ungated hover motion, or missing reduced-motion behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill decide when motion is unnecessary?
faq.answer: Yes. It can reject animation for frequent actions, keyboard workflows, or motion without a clear purpose.

faq.question: Which animation tools can it use?
faq.answer: It can choose CSS transitions, CSS animations, the Web Animations API, or Motion.

faq.question: Does it support reduced-motion preferences?
faq.answer: Yes. Each implementation should include a gentler variant that removes unnecessary movement while preserving useful state feedback.

faq.question: Can it build accessible dropdowns or dialogs from scratch?
faq.answer: No. It recommends an appropriate component library when focus management and interaction semantics are required.

faq.question: Can it review existing animations?
faq.answer: This skill focuses on construction. A dedicated review or codebase audit skill is more suitable for existing motion.

faq.question: Will every animation be fully tuned from code alone?
faq.answer: No. Crossfades, spring response, and gesture feel may require playback, device testing, and human evaluation.
